messages:
Alex: Proposal: traffic rebalancer + priority queues for feature gates to stabilize canaries in multi-region rollouts. Quick sync? TL;DR: rebalance traffic away from failing variants without full kill, and queue high-priority customer requests into a protected pool.
Jamie: Sounds interesting — do you have the failure modes and rollback triggers sketched out?
Alex: Yep. Three main failure modes: transient latency spikes, persistent model quality degradation, and capacity blowouts. Proposed response:
- transient -> short reroute + observe
- persistent -> tiered fallback (enterprise -> dedicated pool -> open fallback)
- capacity -> priority queue + backpressure shedding
Rollback trigger example: error-rate > 4% for 5m OR P95 latency +20% sustained for 10m -> sweep rollback.
Vijay: Can you dump the draft flag config? A small schema would help implementation.
Alex: Sure, here's the rough flag config we discussed:
```
{
  "flag": "feature_x_rebalancer",
  "modes": ["observe","rebalance","drain","kill"],
  "thresholds": {
    "error_rate_pct": 4,
    "p95_latency_pct_increase": 20,
    "sustained_window_secs": 300
  },
  "priority_pools": ["enterprise","standard","best-effort"]
}
```
Carmen: For A/B tests: how do we slice cohorts so this doesn't bias experiment metrics? We don't want rebalancer to move traffic mid-experiment.
Alex: Good call. Lock cohorts for the experiment duration (configurable), allow rebalancer only on non-experimental traffic or with explicit override flag. Gate A/B traffic by `experiment_locked=true`.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for feature_x_rebalancer started in eu-west-1 (cohort a/b). Monitoring hooks enabled.
Jamie: Suggest adding a "sweep" safety: small traffic pulses across N independent cohorts; if more than 1 cohort trips the rollback conditions we auto-revert. That reduces flukes from noisy cohorts.
Alex: I like sweep pulses. Add a cooldown/hysteresis: require two consecutive sweep failures within 30m to auto-rollback, plus an immediate alert to oncall.
Vijay: Priority queues — implementation note: maintain per-customer token buckets, route high-priority tokens to protected replica set. Pseudocode:
```
if request.customer_tier == "enterprise" and enterprise_bucket.allow():
  route_to(protected_pool)
else:
  enqueue(request) // best-effort queue
```
Carmen: Metrics/observability: we need trace ids for any reroute, and a per-request breadcrumb of which fallback applied. Also need cost guardrails — queues will add memory/ops.
Jamie: Quick cost back-of-envelope: expect +5-8% infra cost for protected pools and queues, but projected incident MTTR reduction ~30% (so net ops savings for big customers).
Alex: Action items:
- Add sweep pulse config + cooldown (Jamie)
- Finalize flag schema + thresholds (Vijay)
- Hook trace ids + fallback breadcrumb to logs (Carmen)
- Draft rollout plan: beta canary next week, 3-week wide rollout if gating passes (Alex)
Alex: @ops-bot can you tag canary logs with `feature_x_rebalancer:canary` and schedule tentative deploy window? Also add an emergency kill switch endpoint to the runbook.
ops-bot: ACK. Tagging enabled. Tentative deploy window created for 2026-04-01 06:00 UTC. Emergency kill endpoint: `/api/v1/flags/feature_x_rebalancer/kill` (requires SRE auth).
